lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What do you learn from standing behind an olive kiosk for two days at a food expo? Quite a lot, as it turns out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Expo Manger Santé 2023, at Place des Congrès in Montreal. Antoine worked the olive kiosk and also walked the aisles with a notebook, so he saw both the vendor side and the visitor side.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: About 300 dollars over the two days. What worked was short tastings with a story, like where the olives come from and what's in the brine. Repeat visitors on day two helped too, and so did a simple line: try this one if you like that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So samples in small cups, I guess.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, one bite makes people commit. Price cards at eye level, and restocking the best seller for day two, because Saturday's crowd buys what they tasted on Friday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Gen V lettuces, crisp enough to stand out after a day of crackers and dips. The Mate Libre kiosk next door, where the matéina line became a find he told friends about. And Wise smoothie mixes, green and red, which are great for rushed mornings.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Anything about the design of the booths?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: BKind had a clean display, with a readable ingredients panel and no visual shouting, so he took a photo of it. Photos from the hall are credited to OS7Media.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So a trade show is basically a tasting menu with a lesson in selling.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The full post has the photos and the kiosk tips.
